summary: Iter22 — security & stability hardening verified. All 5 fixes (P1.1 NameError in slippage_veto path, P1.2 credentialed CORS allowlist, P1.3 reveal endpoint requires password + audit log + include_master gate, P2.1 broker_deals catches DuplicateKeyError specifically, P2.2 invalid ObjectId → 404) PASS. 9/9 iter22 spec tests pass; 9/9 additional live HTTP verification tests pass (88/88 full regression incl. iter18-iter21 + safety_guardian + max_concurrent_race + iter22 suite). CRITICAL: Found a BREAKING-CHANGE frontend caller at /app/frontend/src/pages/Accounts.jsx line 559 that posts to /credentials/reveal with NO body — this will now 422 in the UI (main agent must update frontend to prompt for password and pass {password, include_master?}).

minor.issue: K8s ingress in front of FastAPI rewrites ACAO to '*' on actual (non-OPTIONS) responses while keeping `access-control-allow-credentials: true` from the app — i.e. the deployed response carries BOTH wildcard origin AND credentials, which browsers refuse. The app-level CORS is correct (verified by hitting localhost:8001 directly: evil origin OPTIONS → 400 no ACAO; whitelisted → 200 with ACAO=trusted + credentials:true). Net effect on security: SAFE (browsers refuse cookies on wildcard ACAO) but technically inconsistent. May want to align ingress to honor app CORS headers.

minor.endpoint: Multiple route modules still call ObjectId() directly
minor.issue: parse_object_id was added to bridge/account/trade routes per spec, but bot_routes.py (~30 occurrences), nl_routes.py, signal_routes.py, affiliate_routes.py, bugs_routes.py, safety_blocks_routes.py still use raw ObjectId() on user-supplied IDs. Some are wrapped in try/except (bugs/affiliate/safety_blocks) but bot_routes.py is mostly unwrapped — garbage account_id on /api/bot/* endpoints can still 500. Not in P2.2 scope but worth a follow-up iter.

ui_bugs.issue: BREAKING CHANGE NOT PROPAGATED. Line 559 calls `api.post(/accounts/${account.id}/credentials/reveal)` with NO request body. The endpoint now requires `{password: str, include_master?: bool}` (Pydantic 422 otherwise). The Reveal button in the Accounts page will no longer work — user will see formatApiError(e) with a 422 validation error. Main agent must (a) add a password prompt modal/dialog before the call and (b) optionally add an 'include master password' checkbox.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend → backend contract drift on POST /api/accounts/{id}/credentials/reveal (was: no body; now: required body). Only one frontend caller found (Accounts.jsx:559).

action_items: Update /app/frontend/src/pages/Accounts.jsx CredentialsPanel.reveal() to prompt for the user's password (and optionally an include_master checkbox) before POSTing to /credentials/reveal. Without this fix, the Reveal button in the Accounts page is broken (returns 422).

OPTIONAL follow-up: migrate remaining raw ObjectId() calls in bot_routes.py, nl_routes.py, signal_routes.py, affiliate_routes.py to parse_object_id from /app/backend/route_utils.py — currently /api/bot/* endpoints with garbage account_id may still return 500.

OPTIONAL: review whether the K8s ingress should pass through the app's CORS headers instead of overwriting ACAO to '*'. Current behavior is safe (browsers refuse wildcard+credentials) but inconsistent with the app's intent.
critical_code_review_comments: P1.1 fix is clean: line 472-476 of bridge_routes.py inlines datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() — no more reference to undefined now_iso. AST check + live HTTP both pass.
P1.2 fix in server.py lines 150-169 is textbook: explicit allowlist + credentials, OR wildcard + no credentials, never both. Verified at app layer (localhost:8001 direct).

P1.3 reveal endpoint: defense-in-depth is solid — pydantic body validation (422), ObjectId try/except (404), password re-confirmation via auth.verify_password (403 + audit row), include_master gate, audit log includes wrong_password attempts for brute-force visibility, secrets never appear in audit log. One nit: when account exists but password is wrong, the 403 message ('Password re-confirmation failed') differs from the 404 ('Account not found') — this discloses account existence. Minor info leak; OK for owner-only endpoint.
P2.1 fix at bridge_routes.py:577-586 is correct: DuplicateKeyError → 200 duplicate:true; any other Exception → logger.exception + raise HTTPException(500). No silent swallow.

P2.2 fix is partial — parse_object_id added to bridge/account/trade routes, but ~30 other ObjectId() call sites remain across bot_routes/nl_routes/signal_routes/affiliate_routes. Spec only required the routes called out so this is in-scope, but flagging for completeness.
route_utils.parse_object_id is a clean abstraction (404 on InvalidId/TypeError/ValueError/empty) — recommend adopting across the codebase.

rca of the issue: P1.1: NameError caused by orphaned `now_iso` reference inside slippage_veto branch where the variable was never defined in that scope — fixed by inlining datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(). P1.2: original `allow_origin_regex='.*' + allow_credentials=True` was a textbook credentialed-CORS misconfig — any malicious page could read authenticated responses. Fixed by branching CORS config on CORS_ORIGINS env. P1.3: original endpoint returned all stored creds (including master) to any holder of a valid session, with no audit trail — fixed via pydantic body w/ password re-confirmation, include_master gate, and unconditional audit log. P2.1: bare `except Exception:` masked all insert failures as duplicates, losing real broker fills — fixed by narrowing to DuplicateKeyError and raising 500 on other exceptions. P2.2: ObjectId() raises InvalidId on malformed strings which surfaces as 500 — fixed via shared route_utils.parse_object_id helper that returns 404 with a clean resource label.
